resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §45 line 157: harm: The count is right, but the finding shouldn't block. I counted curriculum/exercises/extract-the-task-shaping-rule.md L157-161 myself: the label says "three observable verbs" and four bullets follow. git blame shows how it drifted. The rule (L158) and loading-mechanism (L160) bullets date from 2026-05-15 (1ff6f8a4). The rules-file-first bullet (L161) came on 2026-07-26 (fe182973). The story-ticket bullet (L159) came on 2026-08-12 (8db3e1a2, "M1 reads a bug ticket, M2 reads a story ticket, same move"). So the label is stale, but three things stop this from being a BLOCKING finding.

(1) The rule's own blocking condition is not met. check_pedagogy.md §45 (L115) says "Story judge blocks ship on missing/unfalsifiable leap tests" and gives the diagnostic "read leap test in isolation; can a working engineer tell whether they did it Monday?" All four bullets pass that test. Each one is a concrete, checkable act on the engineer's own codebase: adds a rule to a named file, reads a story ticket's fields before shaping work, names the loading mechanism, states the rules-file-first order before asking for a build. None of them is missing, abstract or unfalsifiable. The rule gives no ship-block for having one outcome too many.

(2) Harm lens (a) and (b): nobody in the room is worse off. This is a trainer-only maintainer block, and a trainer reading four good Monday outcomes under a "three" label loses nothing. The stated harm ("the count discipline the rule protects against padding has silently drifted") just restates the rule. §45's text never names padding as its purpose; its purpose is observable rather than competency outcomes, and that purpose is intact.

(3) Harm lens (c): the lead fix makes things worse. It folds the story-ticket bullet into the loading-mechanism bullet. That would produce one compound bullet joining two unrelated behaviours, which is harder to check on Monday. It would also bury the story-ticket outcome the maintainer added deliberately on 2026-08-12 as the M1/M2 parallel. That erases a deliberate beat to fix a label.

At most this is a NON-BLOCKING tidiness note: change "three" to "four" on L157, a one-word maintainer-block edit that needs no card. Or, if the maintainer wants the count held at three, they can choose which bullet to cut. It is not a blocking §45 finding.; pedagogy §16 line 63: scope: The finding is refuted as a BLOCKING finding. The quote is accurate (line 63, an unfenced "ask for the `@import` line before you move on"), and pedagogy §16 does say "Location: in fence, not body." The §16 optional-refinement carve-out does not cover it either, because "before you move on" is a gate. The maintainer block at L120 says so explicitly. So on rule text alone the §16 observation holds.

Lens (c) kills the blocking severity. There is a dated maintainer accept-note that pre-authorises exactly this span. The file's maintainer block (L120) reads "standing [watch], reaffirmed 2026-08-02 ... Accepted as-is ... a pedagogy REVISE here is the expected steady state, not a new finding. Do not fold it into the fence before the trigger fires." curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/pre-cohort-todos.md:38 backs this up: "the pedagogy instance scores §16 REVISE non-blocking by design (class verdict PASS_WITH_TODOS)". The trigger for acting is cohort field evidence, and none exists yet ("cohorts: none yet" in the Quality block).

§16 Boundary 2 (2026-08-02, Antti) also says: "File carries a maintainer accept-note; do not escalate body-ask → new registry prompt without maintainer sign-off." The judge's own fix line agrees: "no action owed; filed non-blocking per the maintainer's own accept-note." A finding whose own remedy is "no action, non-blocking" cannot stand as BLOCKING. Applying it would fold the ask into the fence, which the maintainer block explicitly forbids before the trigger fires. / harm: The finding refutes itself. It is filed as BLOCKING, yet its own fix line says "no action owed; filed non-blocking per the maintainer's own accept-note, not a card". A blocking finding with no fix is not blocking.

What I verified:
- **The line exists.** Line 63 of curriculum/exercises/extract-the-task-shaping-rule.md is a body bullet asking for the `@import` line "before you move on". Grant that §16's "Location: in fence" applies, and that the optional-refinements carve-out does not cover it, since "before you move on" is a gate.
- **The maintainer block settles it.** It sits at L120, not L146 as the judge cited. It calls this a KNOWN §16 gap held open on purpose as a standing [watch], reaffirmed 2026-08-02.
